pharm: Partial agonist at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors and antagonist at 5-HT2A receptors.
quick: Schizophrenia: 10-15 mg once daily; max 30 mg/day
Take once daily without regard to meals
Third-trimester use risks neonatal EPS/withdrawal; use if needed
Present in milk; monitor infant; weigh benefit
Metabolic profile, weight, glucose, lipids, EPS, mood
summary: Aripiprazole is an atypical antipsychotic that acts as a dopamine D2 partial agonist. Oral formulations are indicated for schizophrenia, irritability associated with autistic disorder, and Tourette's disorder. It carries a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (for which it is not approved) and for increased suicidal thoughts/behaviors when used as an adjunct antidepressant in young patients.
indications: Schizophrenia (adults and adolescents 13 years and older)
Irritability associated with autistic disorder (pediatric patients 6-17 years)

dosage.d: Start and target 10-15 mg once daily
dosage.n: Max 30 mg/day; doses above 10-15 mg not more effective

dosage.d: <50 kg: start 2 mg, target 5 mg, max 10 mg/day; >=50 kg: start 2 mg, target 10 mg, max 20 mg/day

dosage.n: Adjust further with CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors or inducers

admin: Administer once daily without regard to meals
Titrate gradually; allow about 2 weeks at a dose to assess response (steady state)
Halve the dose in known CYP2D6 poor metabolizers and with strong CYP2D6/3A4 inhibitors
Increase the dose when used with strong CYP3A4 inducers
moa: Aripiprazole's efficacy is thought to be mediated by partial agonism at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors combined with antagonism at 5-HT2A receptors. As a D2 partial agonist it stabilizes dopaminergic tone, reducing activity where dopamine is excessive and supporting it where deficient.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to aripiprazole (reactions from urticaria to anaphylaxis)
relative: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning, not approved)
History of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, or dyslipidemia

preg: Neonates exposed in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms after delivery. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; consider enrollment in the National Pregnancy Registry for Atypical Antipsychotics.
lact: Aripiprazole is present in human milk; consider the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding alongside maternal need and any adverse effects on the infant. Monitor the infant for sedation, irritability, and feeding difficulties.
renal: No dosage adjustment required for renal impairment.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment required for hepatic impairment.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin): reduce aripiprazole dose by half
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine): reduce dose by half
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin): double the aripiprazole dose
moderate: Other CNS depressants and alcohol (additive sedation)
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals.
interactions.diagnostics: May affect prolactin and metabolic laboratory values.

serious: Pathological gambling and other impulse-control problems

monitoring: Weight, BMI, fasting glucose, and lipids at baseline and periodically
counsel: May take about 2 weeks to see the full effect; do not stop on your own
Report new or compulsive urges (gambling, shopping, eating, sex)
Rise slowly to avoid dizziness; avoid alcohol
Watch for restlessness, abnormal movements, fever with stiffness, or thoughts of self-harm
Attend appointments for weight, blood sugar, and cholesterol checks
pk: Antipsychotic effect over days to weeks
pearls: D2 partial agonist (dopamine stabilizer) rather than a pure antagonist
Lower risk of prolactin elevation than many antipsychotics
Long half-life means steady state takes ~2 weeks
Watch for impulse-control disorders, which resolve on dose reduction or discontinuation
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered; if it is close to the next dose, skip it. Do not double up. Because of the long half-life, occasional missed doses have limited immediate effect, but consistency matters.
overdose: Reported features include lethargy, somnolence, vomiting, agitation, and tachycardia; serious outcomes are uncommon. No specific antidote; provide supportive care, airway protection, ECG monitoring, and activated charcoal if early. Aripiprazole is not significantly dialyzable.
